tagline: The 'Cusco of the North' guards the room where the last Inca emperor was held for ransom, ringed by pre-Inca ruins, thermal baths and one of South America's wildest Carnivals.
overview: Cajamarca is where the Inca Empire ended. In 1532, conquistadors captured Atahualpa here in an ambush in the main square; the emperor offered to fill his room with gold for his freedom, and the Ransom Room still stands beside the plaza.

The highland city (2,750m) keeps a beautiful colonial centre of Baroque churches and carved stone, but the bigger draw is the country around it. The Baños del Inca thermal baths still flow where the Inca once soaked, and the ancient canals and stone forest of Cumbemayo crown the hills outside town.

Cajamarca hosts Peru's rowdiest Carnival — weeks of water fights, music and parades each February. The surrounding countryside holds the Otuzco cliff tombs, the hilltop church of Santa Apolonia with its city view, and farms making the region's famous cheeses.

funFacts.text: Atahualpa offered to fill a room once with gold and twice with silver — the room still stands.
